articles.title: Women who kill their partners are often judged through “mad, bad or sad” stereotypes, review finds
articles.summary: Are women who kill their partners judged on the facts, or on assumptions about how women should behave? A review of 24 studies suggests gender stereotypes still color how jurors, judges, and journalists see them.

articles.title: ADHD symptoms may reflect a brain shifting toward overly synchronized activity, study suggests
articles.summary: The brain may work best near a tipping point between disorder and excessive synchrony. A new study suggests ADHD symptoms could reflect individual differences in where each person’s brain operates relative to that point.

articles.title: Republicans much more likely to think Tylenol in pregnancy is tied to autism, no matter how the question is asked
articles.summary: Whether a poll asked if Tylenol “causes,” “increases the risk” of, or is “linked” to autism made little difference to how Americans answered, a new experiment finds. Political party mattered far more.

articles.title: Group therapy helps autistic teenagers navigate dating and sexuality
articles.summary: A newly developed group training program helps autistic teenagers safely learn about romantic relationships, personal boundaries, and sexual health. By practicing social skills with peers, teenagers can improve their understanding of intimacy and reduce inappropriate behaviors.

articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? articles.title: Common osteoporosis drugs linked to 24% lower dementia risk in major study
articles.summary: A massive study of more than 120,000 older adults suggests that common osteoporosis drugs may reduce the risk of Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias by up to 24%. The surprising findings raise the possibility that medications already used to strengthen bones could also help protect the aging brain.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden warning sign of cannabis addiction
articles.summary: A study of more than 17,700 US adults found that people who use cannabis in multiple forms have dramatically higher rates of daily consumption and addiction symptoms than those who stick primarily to one method. Nearly 67% of those who used almost every form met criteria for cannabis use disorder, compared with just 15% of people who mainly consumed edibles.

articles.title: An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin
articles.summary: A surprising new study suggests that an anti-aging drug could help protect people genetically predisposed to Alzheimer's disease. Researchers found that just four weeks of low-dose rapamycin improved brain blood flow in healthy middle-aged adults carrying the high-risk APOE4 gene variant, with women showing the strongest benefits. Because declining blood flow can occur years before Alzheimer's symptoms appear, the discovery raises hopes for preventing or delaying the disease before memory loss begins.

articles.title: Spiking neuromodulation: a linear control perspective
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.08571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neuronal excitability is a nonlinear phenomenon, and the complexity of spiking experimental traces sometimes looks defeating. The present paper takes the view point that excitability is a neuromodulated property, and aims to demonstrate that the neuromodulation of spiking is amenable to the classical linear analysis tools of control theory. We illustrate the value of linear feedback analysis as an alternative to bifurcation analysis in the simple yet classical example of spiking modulation by the A-type potassium current.
